title: Databricks model resources: a new resource type needs an enum member, a DatabricksResource subclass, and a _get_resource_class_by_type entry; model-version dependency wiring is separate and deferred
answers: How do I declare a Unity Catalog model service dependency when logging a model?
Why doesn't my new Databricks dependency type show up in the logged model's resources in MLmodel?
Where are Databricks resource types mapped to their classes for MLmodel serialization?
Why isn't UC model-version registration sending my model service dependency?
body:
Path: mlflow/models/resources.py:_get_resource_class_by_type and the Databricks resource classes (DatabricksVectorSearchIndex, DatabricksServingEndpoint, DatabricksUCConnection, DatabricksApp, DatabricksLakebase, DatabricksUCModelService). This is the resource-declaration path used when a model is logged with `resources=`: each declared dependency is serialized into the MLmodel `resources` section and rebuilt from YAML or dict via _ResourceBuilder.
Rule: To add a Databricks dependency type, (1) add a ResourceType enum member with a snake_case wire value (ResourceType.UC_MODEL_SERVICE = "uc_model_service"), (2) add a DatabricksResource subclass whose `type` property returns that member and whose __init__ calls super() with the name and on_behalf_of_user, and (3) register its wire value in the "databricks" map inside _get_resource_class_by_type. Steps 1-3 together give to_dict/from_dict and YAML round-trip. Do not add it to UC model-version dependency registration (get_model_version_dependencies in mlflow/store/_unity_catalog/registry/rest_store.py) until the backend CreateModelVersionRequest DependencyType proto accepts the new type, because an unknown type there fails registration.
Constraints: Applies to resource metadata declared at model logging time. It does not change model-version dependency registration, and existing types such as serving_endpoint stay as they are for backward compatibility.
applies: Adding or changing Databricks resource declarations for logged models (MLmodel resources); not UC model-version dependency registration.
says: A declared model service dependency is missing from the logged model resource metadata.
Support declaring model service dependencies when logging models to the catalog.
The logged model does not display the attached service in its resource list.
Registering a model version fails because the new dependency type is not recognized.
Custom service dependencies specified during model logging are dropped from the model details.
search: Adding a Databricks model dependency type requires adding a snake_case ResourceType enum member, a DatabricksResource subclass returning that type, and an entry in _get_resource_class_by_type. This enables YAML and dictionary serialization for dependencies declared under resources= at model logging time. Do not wire the new dependency into Unity Catalog model-version registration in get_model_version_dependencies until the backend CreateModelVersionRequest DependencyType proto supports it, or registration will fail. The rule applies to logged model resource metadata, leaving existing types like serving_endpoint unchanged for backward compatibility.
